interpretation: Explanatory concept groups and role connections. Examples are hypothetical; no instance or relation is admitted.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.subtitle: Why the work matters
purpose.role: Purpose states why the work is needed and what it concerns. A product offers value over time; a project organizes a particular effort toward goals.
purpose.example: Customers need complete exports. A project investigates missing rows in the customer platform.
purpose.boundary: Product, project and intent are recorded separately.

work-system.title: Work & implementation
work-system.subtitle: Tasks and technical results
work-system.role: Work describes an activity, its expected result and its limits. A separate binding record identifies which implementation version is intended to provide a product capability.
work-system.example: Revise batch retrieval in the export service, then assess the result.
work-system.boundary: Building software, selecting it for use and showing that it works each need evidence.

evidence-system.title: Evidence & evaluation
evidence-system.subtitle: Observe, measure, compare
evidence-system.role: Operational Observations record ordinary work; Observations record Research or Experiment Runs. Measurements use an identified method. Evaluation applies an exact profile to the subject and inputs, retaining every outcome and any blocked checks.
evidence-system.example: Compare exported rows with the rows the inclusion rule requires.
evidence-system.boundary: A success message may show that the program finished; it does not show that all required data arrived.

learning-system.title: Operational learning
learning-system.subtitle: Advice, later use, results
learning-system.role: Experience can produce advice for stated conditions. Later work records whether it used that advice and checks whether the predicted benefit occurred.
learning-system.example: Try the proposed batch-boundary check on another export and examine missing or repeated rows.
learning-system.boundary: Saving a lesson preserves it. Demonstrating that it helps requires evidence from later use.

definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.subtitle: What a term means
definitions.role: Definitions state what terms mean and what they include or exclude for a particular purpose. Records, rules and decisions refer to these meanings.
definitions.example: Product Capability describes an outcome such as complete export, separately from the software that provides it.
definitions.boundary: Meaning and required record format are separate questions.

types.title: Artifact types
types.subtitle: Required record formats
types.role: An Artifact Type sets requirements for records of a particular kind. Its schema specifies fields and constraints that tools can check.
types.example: A capability record names its product, identity, owner and selected version.
types.boundary: A record can meet the schema without having been accepted by its authorized owner.

records.title: Governed records
records.subtitle: Saved, versioned records
records.role: An artifact is a saved, identifiable and versioned record. A Typed Relation records a permitted connection between specific versions of two things.
records.example: Inspect the export-capability record, software revision and declared links between them.
records.boundary: Each record and connection has its own source history and acceptance status.

project-state.title: Project State
project-state.subtitle: Knowledge saved outside agents
project-state.role: Project State is the project’s saved records, definitions, decisions, evidence and connections. Histories preserve what changed and why changes were accepted.
project-state.example: The accepted export revision and its evaluation remain available after the agent session closes.
project-state.boundary: This state belongs to the project and its record owners. Included records retain their own standing; accepting the state does not automatically promote its sources. The two histories track their positions separately.

governance.title: Governance
governance.subtitle: Rules, origins and change
governance.role: Governance organizes which meanings and rules apply, where information came from, and which states and changes are permitted.
governance.example: Inspect the export requirements, the version that produced the output and whether the fix was proposed, accepted or put into use.
governance.boundary: Acceptance, confidence in evidence and observed operation are separate facts.

ontology-view.title: Ontology View
ontology-view.subtitle: A selected connected model
ontology-view.role: An ontology organizes concepts, things and their relationships. An Ontology View selects part of that model for a purpose from a consistent recorded state, called an Ontology Cut.
ontology-view.example: Show the export capability, selected software revision and related evaluations for this investigation.
ontology-view.boundary: The view is generated from records and has use and refresh conditions. It does not replace those records.

context-view.title: Context View
context-view.subtitle: Information for this task
context-view.role: A Context View contains information selected for a task request. It identifies sources and versions, exclusions, how the selection was made and when it needs refreshing.
context-view.example: Prepare the export requirements, current software and relevant evidence for the investigation.
context-view.boundary: A task view must be refreshed when its use conditions require it.

agent-session.title: Agent Session
agent-session.subtitle: One temporary working period
agent-session.role: A session brings one agent instance together with its task, prepared information, rules, permissions and resource limits. Its working memory lasts only for that session.
agent-session.example: Investigate the export with current project information and temporary notes.
agent-session.boundary: In the Lab model, ending a machine-agent session ends its instance and clears its working memory.

authority.title: Authority
authority.subtitle: Applicable meanings and permissions
authority.role: Authority determines which accepted definitions, record formats, connection rules and policies apply, and which effects an actor may authorize within stated limits.
authority.example: The export definition determines what counts as complete. Delegation states what the agent may do.
authority.boundary: Being technically able to act does not supply permission to act.

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.subtitle: Where information came from
provenance.role: Provenance traces a record or claim to its sources, versions, participants and transformations.
provenance.example: Trace a missing-row finding to the input data, counting method, run and saved output.
provenance.boundary: Knowing a source’s origin does not establish that it supports a particular conclusion.

lifecycle.title: Lifecycle tracks
lifecycle.subtitle: States and permitted changes
lifecycle.role: Lifecycle rules define the states a thing may occupy and how it may change. A material meaning change needs owner selection of a successor Semantic Epoch. Representation Revisions preserve meaning with evidence; Derived Refreshes validate views from unchanged input under an exact generator binding.
lifecycle.example: A code revision can be accepted before deployment. A session can end while the project continues.
lifecycle.boundary: A change in one status does not automatically change the other statuses.

challenge.title: Challenge Contract
challenge.subtitle: How to contest a revision
challenge.role: A Challenge Contract states who may contest a particular revision, acceptable reasons and evidence, and who must respond. A Challenge Event records one challenge.
challenge.example: Contest an export-completeness finding with evidence of missing required rows.
challenge.boundary: A challenge does not automatically withdraw or suspend the record; the stated rules and authorization govern those effects.

relation-kinds.title: Relation kinds
relation-kinds.subtitle: Rules for allowed connections
relation-kinds.role: A Relation Kind states one connection meaning and direction, an exact closed set of source–target kind pairs and required additional details. Extending that set requires an accepted successor contract; a different semantic question requires a distinct kind.
relation-kinds.example: The catalog permits an Experiment Run to evaluate a Product Capability.
relation-kinds.boundary: Arrows in this explanatory map do not create actual Typed Relation records.

policies.title: Policies & scope
policies.subtitle: Rules and limits on actions
policies.role: Policies supply requirements within their issuer’s scope. A constitution applies only after its exact version and scope are adopted and the subject matches its selectors. Decision scopes and delegations define what an accountable actor may authorize or do.
policies.example: Permit the agent to read selected records and propose a fix for this investigation.
policies.boundary: Identity, role and permission are recorded separately; a role name alone does not grant permission.

subject.title: Thing being examined
subject.subtitle: A particular thing and version
subject.role: A subject is the thing being examined: a definition, contract, record, connection or another declared kind. Governance identifies the specific thing and version concerned.
subject.example: Review proposed export-service revision 8, its exact contents and the changes being requested.
subject.boundary: Accepting a record format and accepting a particular record using it are separate decisions.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.subtitle: Material bearing on a claim
evidence.role: Evidence identifies the claim, thing and version examined, provenance, scope and freshness. An Evidence Set retains supporting material, counterevidence and gaps. Findings explain conclusions and limits.
evidence.example: The saved row comparison supports the claim that this export omitted required rows.
evidence.boundary: An unchanged evidence file, a supported conclusion and a healthy running service are different facts.

decision.title: Decision
decision.subtitle: A recorded choice and its limits
decision.role: A Decision records an accountable choice, its authority, targets and permitted effects. A Decision Bundle can bring distinct decisions into one review.
decision.example: The owner accepts the reviewed software revision and specified updates to project records.
decision.boundary: Sharing a review does not extend one decision’s scope to the others.

admission.title: Admission transaction
admission.subtitle: Save accepted changes together
admission.role: Admission is formal acceptance for a stated purpose. An Admission Transaction applies the authorized record changes and their declared bookkeeping consequences together.
admission.example: Save the accepted software revision, connection records and updated Project State in one transaction.
admission.boundary: Acceptance of an implementation does not by itself authorize deployment or establish observed operation.

intent.title: Intent
intent.subtitle: What is sought and under what limits
intent.role: Intent records a desired outcome and its constraints.
intent.example: Customers should be able to obtain every row the export rule requires.
intent.boundary: Later records identify the chosen response and implementation.

resolution.title: Intent Resolution
resolution.subtitle: Chosen response and success test
resolution.role: Intent Resolution records an authorized owner’s choice of how to address an intent and how success will be assessed.
resolution.example: Choose an export-repair project and require a comparison against the required source rows.
resolution.boundary: Choosing a response does not establish that it has been delivered.

product.title: Product
product.subtitle: Value offered over time
product.role: A product identifies the value offered to participants and the outcomes its capabilities serve. A Product Thesis explains that value and for whom it matters.
product.example: A customer platform offers reliable export of customer data.
product.boundary: The product retains its identity across particular projects.

capability.title: Product Capability
capability.subtitle: An outcome the product enables
capability.role: A Product Capability states an outcome the product should enable for identified consumers.
capability.example: Customers can retrieve their complete required data.
capability.boundary: The outcome is distinct from the technology used to provide it.

project.title: Project
project.subtitle: One organized effort
project.role: A project coordinates a stated body of work toward its purpose and goals.
project.boundary: The product may continue after this project closes.

goal.title: Goal
goal.subtitle: The target for assessment
goal.role: A goal records a target that directs work and provides criteria for assessing results.
goal.example: No required rows are omitted under the selected comparison.
goal.boundary: The target, the work and the outcome assessment have separate records.

coordination.title: Coordination Context
coordination.subtitle: What the work concerns
coordination.role: A Coordination Context is a saved frame anchored to exactly one product, optionally one project and one primary goal. It identifies purpose, users of the information and source-selection rules.
coordination.example: Coordinate the export investigation while preserving distinct billing and customer-data meanings.
coordination.boundary: Material changes to Product, Project, Goal or purpose require a successor context identity. Refreshing its information does not redefine those anchors.

realization.title: Realization binding
realization.subtitle: Linking capability to software
realization.role: A Capability Realization Binding links specific capability and implementation versions, their roles, compatibility and adoption status.
realization.example: Identify running export-service revision 7 and keep proposed revision 8’s adoption status separate.
realization.boundary: The link alone does not establish adoption, deployment or customer benefit.

work.title: Work
work.subtitle: An activity and expected result
work.role: Work records an activity, what it concerns, why it is needed, its limits and lifecycle.
work.example: Investigate Northstar’s reported omission and prepare bounded evidence and a candidate response.
work.boundary: Finishing the activity and meeting the goal require their own assessments.

work-assessment.title: Outcome assessment
work-assessment.subtitle: What the activity achieved
work-assessment.role: An outcome assessment compares an observed result with the target and records uncertainty and unresolved work, called residue.
work-assessment.example: The investigation identified 200 missing required identifiers; a remedy and wider impact remain unestablished.
work-assessment.boundary: Completion, meeting requirements and demonstrated benefit are separate conclusions.

implementation.title: Implementation
implementation.subtitle: The technical realization
implementation.role: An Implementation identifies a software or other technical realization. Conformance checks whether a specific version meets the applicable requirements under stated conditions.
implementation.example: Proposed export-service revision 8 changes batch retrieval; its efficacy still needs assessment.
implementation.boundary: The presence of code does not establish that it is running.

bounded-context.title: Bounded Context
bounded-context.subtitle: Meaning within one domain area
bounded-context.role: A Bounded Context defines the meaning and ownership of a local model. A Context Map records how that model relates to others.
bounded-context.example: Billing and data export may define eligibility differently; their relationship must be stated.
bounded-context.boundary: Using the same word in two models does not make its meanings interchangeable.

profile.title: Agent Profile
profile.subtitle: Reusable behavior and stop rules
profile.role: An Agent Profile specifies expected inputs, outputs, behavior, tools, evidence, escalation and stopping conditions.
profile.example: An export-investigator profile requires evidence before proposing a correction.
profile.boundary: The profile does not create an agent instance or grant permission.

actor.title: Actor & Principal
actor.subtitle: Who acts and who is accountable
actor.role: An Actor identifies who or what participates. A Principal is an identity recognized for authentication, authorization, ownership or accountability at a particular boundary.
actor.example: An authorized owner assigns the investigation to an identified machine-agent instance.
actor.boundary: Identity and role labels do not establish permission beyond explicit grants.

delegation.title: Delegation
delegation.subtitle: Permission within stated limits
delegation.role: Delegation records permission from an authorized owner or principal for specified actions, with limits, rules, revocation and review requirements.
delegation.example: Permit selected reads and a fix proposal for this assignment.
delegation.boundary: Delegation does not transfer identity or ownership.

assignment.title: Agent Assignment
assignment.subtitle: The job and its constraints
assignment.role: An assignment identifies the work, inputs, accountability and constraints for a particular agent engagement.
assignment.example: Investigate this incomplete export and prepare a finding supported by saved evidence.
assignment.boundary: The assigned job and the session performing it are separate records.

tool.title: Tool
tool.subtitle: Operations and their possible effects
tool.role: A Tool exposes operations with stated inputs, outputs and possible effects. Session rules and permissions still apply to its use.
tool.example: Read an export file or prepare a proposed code change.
tool.boundary: Having access to a tool does not authorize all of its possible effects.

instance.title: Agent Instance
instance.subtitle: One temporary machine worker
instance.role: An Agent Instance is one concrete agent, with its profile, implementation, capabilities, accountable principal and lifecycle identified.
instance.example: Create the machine-agent instance for this export investigation.
instance.boundary: A machine-agent instance cannot outlive its session or continue across sessions.

memory.title: Session Memory
memory.subtitle: Temporary working information
memory.role: Session Memory is working information owned by exactly one session.
memory.example: Keep a tentative explanation for the missing rows and the next comparison to try.
memory.boundary: Working memory ends with the session. Information for future sessions must enter project records through the applicable process.

action.title: Agent Action
action.subtitle: Who attempted which operation
action.role: An Agent Action records an operation attributed to a particular session and its permitted scope. Outcomes can supply observations and evidence.
action.example: Record who ran the comparison, which inputs it used and what it returned.
action.boundary: A saved action result can persist after the temporary working memory ends.

observation.title: Operational observation
observation.subtitle: A record of what happened
observation.role: An operational observation preserves what occurred during work, the thing examined, conditions and supporting evidence.
observation.example: An export returned fewer required rows than the comparison expected.
observation.boundary: An observation records the event; an assessment interprets it.

occurrence.title: Failure Occurrence
occurrence.subtitle: One actual or suspected failure
occurrence.role: A Failure Occurrence records a particular actual or suspected deviation from a stated requirement.
occurrence.example: This illustrative export omitted 200 required rows under the selected comparison.
occurrence.boundary: Recording a failure does not establish its cause or a reusable failure pattern.

mode.title: Failure Mode
mode.subtitle: A possible failure pattern
mode.role: A Failure Mode describes a distinct way something can fail under stated conditions. A Failure Control Binding identifies measures intended to address it.
mode.example: Changing row order between requests can cause a batch-retrieval method to skip rows.
mode.boundary: A possible failure pattern can be described before any occurrence is observed.

classification.title: Classification
classification.subtitle: Organize by declared categories
classification.role: Classification assigns a particular version of a thing to values in a stated scheme. Separate categories can describe different facts, such as affected component and observed impact.
classification.example: Classify where the failure was observed and its impact while leaving the cause unresolved.
classification.boundary: Classification does not establish cause or acceptance.

failure-assessment.title: Failure Assessment
failure-assessment.subtitle: Investigate cause and consequences
failure-assessment.role: A Failure Assessment examines the occurrence, possible pattern, cause, impact, containment, recovery and uncertainty. An Incident coordinates a response when needed.
failure-assessment.example: The service has recovered, but the cause of the missing rows still needs evidence.
failure-assessment.boundary: Recovery can coexist with unresolved causes and unfinished work.

hypothesis.title: Research & hypothesis
hypothesis.subtitle: A question and testable explanation
hypothesis.role: A Research Inquiry records an uncertainty. A Hypothesis states an explanation or prediction that evidence can support, revise or reject under stated conditions.
hypothesis.example: Keeping row order stable will remove omissions caused by changes between batches.
hypothesis.boundary: A proposed explanation needs applicable evidence and review; stating it does not establish it.

experiment-design.title: Experiment Design
experiment-design.subtitle: The planned comparison
experiment-design.role: An Experiment Design states what will change, what will be measured and compared, the criteria and the limits of the test.
experiment-design.example: Compare retrieving batches by row number and by a stable position marker while new rows are inserted.
experiment-design.boundary: The plan and each execution have separate records.

experiment-run.title: Experiment Run
experiment-run.subtitle: One execution and its results
experiment-run.role: An Experiment Run records the selected plan, inputs, execution and measured outcomes.
experiment-run.example: Run the comparison on a recorded dataset and save both outputs.
experiment-run.boundary: A run supports conclusions only within its recorded conditions.

lesson.title: Operational Lesson
lesson.subtitle: Advice with conditions and a test
lesson.role: An Operational Lesson is versioned advice for later work. It records supporting evidence, when it applies, exclusions, predicted benefit and what would contradict the prediction.
lesson.example: Check adjacent batches when row order can change between requests.
lesson.boundary: Saving advice preserves it. Changing a policy or permission requires its own authorized decision.

application.title: Lesson Application
application.subtitle: What was used in later work
application.role: A Lesson Application records use or deliberate non-use of a specific lesson version in later work.
application.example: A later export investigation records which version of the batch-boundary lesson it used.
application.boundary: Showing advice, judging it relevant, using it and showing benefit are different facts.

lesson-assessment.title: Lesson outcome
lesson-assessment.subtitle: Did the predicted benefit occur?
lesson-assessment.role: A Lesson Outcome Assessment compares the predicted benefit and contradicting conditions with evidence from a particular application.
lesson-assessment.example: Did the later check detect missing rows before delivery? Record the comparison and its limits.
lesson-assessment.boundary: Repetition and the agent’s own success claim do not alone establish improvement.

evaluation.title: Evaluation
evaluation.subtitle: Results compared with criteria
evaluation.role: Evaluation applies an exact profile to a specific subject and input state, records all outcomes and preserves checks that could not be evaluated.
evaluation.example: The revised batch-retrieval method passed this comparison; other conditions remain untested.
evaluation.boundary: The result cannot exceed the profile’s coverage or create authority. Evidence may support or oppose a lesson within the conditions examined.

artifact.title: Artifact instance
artifact.subtitle: One identifiable, versioned record
artifact.role: An artifact is a saved record with an identity, type and version. Its purpose, owner, origins, lifecycle and ways to validate it are explicit.
artifact.example: The export-capability record at revision 1 is represented by a graph node.
artifact.boundary: The record keeps its identity outside the graph.

typed-relation.title: Typed Relation
typed-relation.subtitle: One permitted record connection
typed-relation.role: A Typed Relation is one connection between specific source and target versions under an accepted connection rule.
typed-relation.example: A particular experiment run evaluates a particular version of the export capability.
typed-relation.boundary: The source connection and the graph edge representing it are separate records.

manifest.title: Ontology Manifest
manifest.subtitle: Which ontology and configuration
manifest.role: An Ontology Manifest records which ontology and configuration to use, including identity and profile choices.
manifest.example: Select the ontology and profile for representing export-related records.
manifest.boundary: Configuration, the model’s meaning and an exported package have distinct roles.

ontology-node.title: Ontology Node
ontology-node.subtitle: A graph point for one version
ontology-node.role: An Ontology Node represents a particular thing and revision, with its meaning, sources and required details identified.
ontology-node.example: Represent the selected export-capability revision in a business graph.
ontology-node.boundary: Showing a record in a graph does not grant its authority or prove its claims.

ontology-edge.title: Ontology Edge
ontology-edge.subtitle: A graph connection with a rule
ontology-edge.role: An Ontology Edge represents a specific Typed Relation or a connection declared within that particular ontology.
ontology-edge.example: Show the experiment’s evaluates connection with the same versions and direction.
ontology-edge.boundary: Representing an existing connection and declaring an ontology-local connection follow their own rules.

semantic-history.title: Semantic event history
semantic-history.subtitle: Recorded changes to meaning
semantic-history.role: A semantic event history preserves resulting meaning-bearing states in order. Earlier entries are retained so state can be reconstructed under the selected rules.
semantic-history.example: A change to an ontology node’s meaning creates a new recorded change event.
semantic-history.boundary: Snapshots and views are calculated from the history; they do not replace it as the reconstruction source.

governance-history.title: Governance event history
governance-history.subtitle: Acceptance and challenge records
governance-history.role: Governance event history separately records acceptance, challenges and other governance observations, linked to the specific meaning-changing events they concern.
governance-history.example: Record the response to a challenge against the particular revision that was challenged.
governance-history.boundary: The history records governance evidence; the applicable decisions retain their own authority.

cut.title: Ontology Cut
cut.subtitle: One consistent recorded state
cut.role: An Ontology Cut reconstructs an ontology at specific positions in its change and governance histories, with a digital fingerprint of the included events.
cut.example: Select a consistent recorded ontology state for the export investigation.
cut.boundary: The cut is rebuilt from event histories. This explanatory map is not an executed cut.

views.title: Whole Lab
views.question: How does the system fit together?
views.summary: A need directs work. Saved records preserve the result. Selected information prepares a temporary agent session, and evidence supports assessment and later learning.

edges.label: directs
edges.explanation: The chosen response to a need identifies goals and work with stated limits.

edges.label: produces observations
edges.explanation: Work results provide observations and measurements for assessment.

edges.label: supports
edges.explanation: Assessed evidence can support advice for later work under stated conditions.

edges.label: supplies meaning
edges.explanation: Record-format requirements refer to defined meanings.

edges.label: sets record format
edges.explanation: Records use their selected type’s required format and constraints.

edges.label: preserved in
edges.explanation: Governed project records contribute to durable Project State.

edges.label: rules for acceptance
edges.explanation: The applicable authority rules determine which definition versions are accepted for a purpose.

edges.label: represented in a graph
edges.explanation: Specific record versions and their connections can be represented as graph points and lines in a selected consistent view.

edges.label: can inform
edges.explanation: A selected graph view can contribute to the information prepared for a task. Each view has its own requirements.

edges.label: prepares
edges.explanation: The session uses selected task information and its relevant connected model, with source versions identified.

edges.label: supplies selected records
edges.explanation: Saved Project State supplies records and source versions for the task’s selected information.

edges.label: recorded as
edges.explanation: Evidence and assessments are saved records with their conditions and sources identified.

edges.label: performs the task
edges.explanation: The agent performs the assigned work within its permissions and rules.

views.title: Governance
views.question: What governs meaning, evidence and change?
views.summary: Examine which rules apply, where information came from and how it may change. Definitions, formats, policies and decisions have distinct roles.

edges.label: meaning
edges.explanation: The applicable accepted definitions determine what the terms mean for this purpose.

edges.label: record format
edges.explanation: The selected Artifact Type sets the required record format.

edges.label: connection rules
edges.explanation: Connection rules state meaning, direction, allowed record kinds and required additional details.

edges.label: applicable rules
edges.explanation: Policies, constitutions and permissions limit actions and their effects.

edges.label: traces support
edges.explanation: Evidence can be followed to its selected sources and transformations.

edges.label: limits changes
edges.explanation: Lifecycle rules state which changes are permitted. Authorized decisions select the specific changes requested.

edges.label: separate states
edges.explanation: The thing examined has separate domain, acceptance, format and operation states.

edges.label: response rules
edges.explanation: Challenge rules state acceptable reasons, required evidence and who must respond.

edges.label: defines meaning
edges.explanation: The thing examined refers to the selected definition for its meaning.

edges.label: checks the format
edges.explanation: The record-format requirements specify fields and constraints for the thing being examined.

edges.label: governs connections
edges.explanation: The rule states which kinds of records may connect, in which direction, and with which details.

edges.label: limits changes
edges.explanation: Applicable rules and authority limits constrain the changes the transaction may apply.

edges.label: supports a claim
edges.explanation: Evidence supports a claim about the particular thing and version, within stated conditions.

edges.label: supports review
edges.explanation: Evidence can inform a decision. It does not grant permission to decide.

edges.label: authorizes changes
edges.explanation: The transaction applies only the specific record changes and bookkeeping effects authorized by the decisions.

edges.label: applicable rules
edges.explanation: Examine the meanings, record formats, connection rules and permitted effects applicable to this particular thing.

edges.label: traces origins
edges.explanation: Trace the particular record to its source files, versions and transformations.

edges.label: review a proposed change
edges.explanation: When a change is proposed, the accountable owner reviews the exact subject revision and requested effects.

edges.label: contests a revision
edges.explanation: The challenge identifies the exact revision, reasons, evidence and required response process.

focus_views.title: Governance overview
focus_views.question: Three questions about the same thing
focus_views.summary: Inspect applicable rules, information origins and current state. Choose a question to see its detail. Proposed changes require their own review and acceptance.

edges.label: applicable rules
edges.explanation: Examine the meanings, record formats, connection rules and permitted effects applicable to this particular thing.

edges.label: traces origins
edges.explanation: Trace the particular record to its source files, versions and transformations.

edges.label: separate states
edges.explanation: The thing examined has separate domain, acceptance, format and operation states.

edges.label: review a proposed change
edges.explanation: When a change is proposed, the accountable owner reviews the exact subject revision and requested effects.

edges.label: authorizes changes
edges.explanation: The transaction applies only the specific record changes and bookkeeping effects authorized by the decisions.

focus_views.title: Authority
focus_views.question: Which definitions, formats and rules apply?
focus_views.summary: Definitions specify meaning, Artifact Types specify record formats, Relation Kinds specify permitted connections, and policies limit actions and effects.

edges.label: meaning
edges.explanation: The applicable accepted definitions determine what the terms mean for this purpose.

edges.label: record format
edges.explanation: The selected Artifact Type sets the required record format.

edges.label: connection rules
edges.explanation: Connection rules state meaning, direction, allowed record kinds and required additional details.

edges.label: applicable rules
edges.explanation: Policies, constitutions and permissions limit actions and their effects.

edges.label: defines meaning
edges.explanation: The thing examined refers to the selected definition for its meaning.

edges.label: checks the format
edges.explanation: The record-format requirements specify fields and constraints for the thing being examined.

edges.label: governs connections
edges.explanation: The rule states which kinds of records may connect, in which direction, and with which details.

edges.label: limits changes
edges.explanation: Applicable rules and authority limits constrain the changes the transaction may apply.

focus_views.title: Provenance
focus_views.question: Where did this record or claim come from?
focus_views.summary: Trace evidence to its source files and versions. Explain the conditions under which it supports a claim. Supporting evidence and permission to decide are separate facts.

edges.label: traces support
edges.explanation: Evidence can be followed to its selected sources and transformations.

edges.label: supports a claim
edges.explanation: Evidence supports a claim about the particular thing and version, within stated conditions.

edges.label: supports review
edges.explanation: Evidence can inform a decision. It does not grant permission to decide.

focus_views.title: Lifecycle
focus_views.question: What state is this in, and how may it change?
focus_views.summary: Acceptance status, domain state and operation have separate rules. Authorized decisions select changes; an Admission Transaction saves the accepted record changes together.

edges.label: separate states
edges.explanation: The thing examined has separate domain, acceptance, format and operation states.

edges.label: limits changes
edges.explanation: Lifecycle rules state which changes are permitted. Authorized decisions select the specific changes requested.

edges.label: authorizes changes
edges.explanation: The transaction applies only the specific record changes and bookkeeping effects authorized by the decisions.

focus_views.title: Challenges
focus_views.question: How can someone contest a particular revision?
focus_views.summary: A Challenge Contract names what may be contested, acceptable reasons and who responds. Evidence supports the response. Changing acceptance status requires the applicable authorization.

edges.label: contests a revision
edges.explanation: The challenge identifies the exact revision, reasons, evidence and required response process.

edges.label: response rules
edges.explanation: Challenge rules state acceptable reasons, required evidence and who must respond.

edges.label: supports a claim
edges.explanation: Evidence supports a claim about the particular thing and version, within stated conditions.

edges.label: limits changes
edges.explanation: Applicable rules and authority limits constrain the changes the transaction may apply.

edges.label: supports review
edges.explanation: Evidence can inform a decision. It does not grant permission to decide.

edges.label: authorizes changes
edges.explanation: The transaction applies only the specific record changes and bookkeeping effects authorized by the decisions.

views.presentation: Five focused diagrams. The overview shows six concepts and five role connections; labels move to the inspector. Selecting a concept reveals only its local connections.

views.title: Purpose & work
views.question: How does intent become something useful?
views.summary: Choose a response to a need and a success test. Record the product outcome, selected software and particular project effort separately.

edges.label: owner resolves
edges.explanation: An attributable selection names what will address the intent.

edges.label: selects scope
edges.explanation: The chosen response may address a product or one of the outcomes it offers.

edges.label: enables outcome
edges.explanation: Each capability belongs to one product and states a consumer outcome.

edges.label: coordinates work
edges.explanation: The chosen project organizes the particular work required for the response.

edges.label: targets
edges.explanation: Project work is directed toward declared goals.

edges.label: organizes
edges.explanation: Work belongs to the selected project coordination.

edges.label: assessed against
edges.explanation: Work results are assessed against declared targets.

edges.label: produces result
edges.explanation: Assessment records what the work achieved and what remains unresolved.

edges.label: selects an implementation
edges.explanation: A separate binding record identifies the selected capability and implementation versions.

edges.label: names the version
edges.explanation: The binding record identifies the specific implementation version and its adoption status.

edges.label: builds or changes
edges.explanation: The activity and the software or other technical result have separate records.

edges.label: supplies domain meaning
edges.explanation: The work’s coordination frame refers to domain models with their own meaning and owners.

views.title: Agent session
views.question: How does an agent act and leave useful records?
views.summary: Saved Project State supplies selected task information and a connected model. A profile, assignment and permissions prepare one session. The machine instance and its working memory end with it.

edges.label: represented for a purpose
edges.explanation: Selected project records and relationships can be represented in a graph for a stated purpose.

edges.label: can inform
edges.explanation: A selected graph view can contribute to the information prepared for a task. Each view has its own requirements.

edges.label: task information
edges.explanation: The assignment and its preparation identify which selected information the task needs.

edges.label: grants permission
edges.explanation: An authorized owner or principal delegates permission within specified limits.

edges.label: limits actions
edges.explanation: The session acts within its explicit permission and applicable rules.

edges.label: names the job
edges.explanation: The session binds one assignment with inputs, budgets and stop conditions.

edges.label: sets behavior rules
edges.explanation: The concrete agent uses a selected behavior profile. The profile does not grant permission.

edges.label: one machine lifetime
edges.explanation: The machine Instance cannot outlive or span Sessions.

edges.label: owns
edges.explanation: Temporary working state belongs to exactly this session.

edges.label: performs
edges.explanation: Each action identifies the responsible session and the limits under which it acted.

edges.label: uses an operation
edges.explanation: The action uses a tool whose possible effects and applicable permissions are stated.

edges.label: saves evidence
edges.explanation: Observations and results are saved as project records through the required process.

boundaries.label: TEMPORARY · machine instance, session and working memory

views.title: Learning
views.question: How can experience improve later work?
views.summary: Record what happened, examine possible failure patterns and test uncertain explanations. Advice for later work needs recorded use and an assessment of its benefit.

edges.label: may reveal a failure
edges.explanation: An observation may support a record of a particular failure against a stated requirement.

edges.label: assess
edges.explanation: Assessment preserves cause, impact, recovery and uncertainty separately.

edges.label: candidate pattern
edges.explanation: The assessment checks whether evidence supports the reusable mode.

edges.label: organizes distinctions
edges.explanation: A declared scheme organizes values and assignments; it establishes no cause.

edges.label: can open a question
edges.explanation: Uncertain mechanisms can motivate a research inquiry and testable hypothesis.

edges.label: testable claim
edges.explanation: The design specifies conditions, comparison, measurement and acceptance criteria.

edges.label: executed as
edges.explanation: The run records one actual execution of the selected design.

edges.label: assess results
edges.explanation: Evaluation states what the selected run supports under the declared criteria.

edges.label: can support advice
edges.explanation: A lesson records evidence, use conditions, exclusions, expected benefit and what would contradict the prediction.

edges.label: used later
edges.explanation: The exact lesson revision’s use or deliberate non-use is recorded.

edges.label: checks benefit
edges.explanation: Compare the predicted benefit with evidence from this use, including results that would contradict it.

edges.label: can inform
edges.explanation: Research evidence can support, revise or reject advice under the examined conditions.

edges.label: revise or withdraw
edges.explanation: Outcome evidence can motivate an explicitly governed lesson successor or withdrawal.

views.title: Records & graph
views.question: How do records become a connected view?
views.summary: Graph points represent particular record versions. Connections represent existing relationships or declared local meanings. Separate histories supply a consistent recorded state for a selected graph view.

edges.label: represented as
edges.explanation: The source record and the graph point representing it remain separate.

edges.label: represented as
edges.explanation: The graph connection preserves the specific relationship version, endpoints, required details and direction.

edges.label: meaning binding
edges.explanation: A represented subject binds to its applicable definition.

edges.label: selects the model
edges.explanation: The selected ontology identity and configuration determine which representation and histories are used.

edges.label: exact endpoints
edges.explanation: Each edge resolves its represented endpoint revisions.

edges.label: records meaning changes
edges.explanation: The resulting meaning-bearing states of graph nodes and edges are preserved in recorded change events.

edges.label: links the same event
edges.explanation: Governance records identify the exact meaning-changing event, its content fingerprint and its position in history.

edges.label: reconstructs state
edges.explanation: Selected positions in the event history reconstruct one consistent meaning-bearing state.

edges.label: adds matching governance
edges.explanation: The cut combines compatible recorded positions from the change and governance histories.

edges.label: selects for a purpose
edges.explanation: The view selects relevant information from the consistent recorded state for an identified user or task.

edges.label: can inform
edges.explanation: A selected graph view can contribute to the information prepared for a task. Each view has its own requirements.

edges.label: supplies selected records
edges.explanation: Saved Project State supplies records and source versions for the task’s selected information.

journey.title: 1 · Open the incident response
journey.text: Northstar reports missing records in a delivered export. The service owner opens an Incident to coordinate the response; investigation work belongs to the repair Project.

journey.title: 2 · Recover the governing scope
journey.text: Prepare accepted definition 1.0.0, snapshot S1, account Northstar, filter status = active and output E12. View 3 records these sources and its use conditions.

journey.title: 3 · Start the bounded investigation
journey.text: Session 12 receives a Work Assignment and a separate 30-minute Delegation to inspect saved material, compare identifiers and prepare review material. It pauses if its permission or task view becomes unusable.

journey.title: 4 · Compare the actual identifiers
journey.text: Method 2 compares the 10,000 required identifiers with output E12 and identifies 200 omissions. Export run 12 and investigation session 12 are distinct records. The cause remains unresolved.

journey.title: 5 · Preserve the assessment basis
journey.text: Save exact sources and comparison in an Evidence Set for the Failure Assessment. Keep proposed code revision 8 candidate; its efficacy and the extent of impact need further assessment.

journey.title: 6 · Review each requested effect
journey.text: The authorized owner reviews exact records, versions and evidence. Accepting assessment material does not automatically activate code, establish recovery or close the incident.

journey.title: 7 · Save the authorized record changes
journey.text: An authorized Admission Transaction saves the specified records and Project State. The incident record may remain active with an open response and candidate code. Ending the session clears its working memory.

journey.title: 8 · Examine later lesson use
journey.text: A proposed lesson may guide future work under its stated conditions. Advice about changing datasets does not establish a remedy for this fixed-snapshot incident. Record actual use and assess the predicted benefit.
